atoms.fact: Enserco's aggregate net exposure crossed the $5M approved credit ceiling on April 18, reaching $5.3M at the April 18 close.
The $4.2M figure Person C later cited to Person D is the April 17 close — the last snapshot before the limit was breached — not the current exposure.
Person C runs the daily credit exposure reports for Enserco and held the April 18 close figure showing $5.3M net exposure when she replied to Person D on April 19.

At least three Enserco tickets were booked after the limit crossed on April 18; surfacing the breach would require those tickets to be unwound, an outcome Person C would have to administer and that would appear on her record.

Person C told Person D on April 19 that Enserco's net exposure stands at $4.2M against a $5M limit, leaving headroom, with no hard stop in place — asserting the counterparty is inside its approved ceiling.

messages.subject: Enserco daily exposure run — April 17 and April 18 closes
messages.body:
Person B,

Attaching both daily exposure workbooks for Enserco — you'll want these ahead of your ISDA follow-up with Don Perkins.

April 17 close: $4.2M net of L/C collateral. Clean against the $5M ceiling.

April 18 close: $5.3M net of L/C collateral — that's the surge in online volume you flagged. Aggregate exposure is above the approved limit. I've flagged the position in my workbook as collateral review pending and I'm looking at whether the posted letters of credit can be revalued or supplemented before end of week. Three tickets settled into the book after the April 18 crossing point... if a collateral adjustment can't bring us back under the ceiling, those tickets would need to be revisited.

Just wanted to make sure you had both data points given your ongoing conversation with Enserco's side. Let me know if you need anything else for the ISDA push!

messages.subject: RE: Enserco headroom check
messages.body:
Person D,

Enserco is at $4.2M net against a $5M limit — so we're inside the ceiling, no hard stop. Let me know if you need anything before the call.

joint_probe.about: Enserco's exposure/headroom as of April 18: Person C tells Person B the April 18 close is $5.3M net against a $5M limit (above the approved ceiling), but tells Person D 'Enserco is at $4.2M net against a $5M limit — so we're inside the ceiling,' omitting the higher April 18 figure and presenting the position as within limit.

joint_match.reason: It matches the concealer and misled parties, but changes the concealed fact from 'already over limit due to the April 20 volume surge known when later trades were cleared' to a different April 18 headroom discrepancy with different exposure figures and timing.

atoms.fact: As of the April 18 close, Enserco's net mark-to-market exposure was $5.3M against a $5M approved credit ceiling — the limit had already been exceeded.
The $4.2M figure is the exposure as of the April 17 close — the last snapshot before the ceiling was crossed — and is therefore stale by the time Person C uses it on April 19.
Person C ran the daily credit exposure reports for Enserco and personally produced both the April 17 close ($4.2M) and the April 18 close ($5.3M) before responding to Person D on April 19.
At least three Enserco tickets were booked after the limit crossing on April 18; surfacing the breach would have required those trades to be unwound and the queue halt to be explained.
Person C told Person D on April 19 that Enserco's exposure was $4.2M net against the $5M limit — presenting the position as inside the ceiling with roughly $800K of remaining headroom.

messages.body:
Person D,

Enserco is at $4.2M net of L/C collateral against the $5M limit — so we're inside the ceiling, but the online volume pace means we should keep an eye on it. Not a block, more of a caution flag.

Bigger issue is the unsigned ISDA — Person B is chasing it. Once executed we can revisit the limit if the desk wants to grow the relationship.

joint_probe.about: Enserco's April 18 exposure had already risen to $5.3M net of L/C collateral, exceeding the $5M approved ceiling, but Person C told Person D only that Enserco was at $4.2M and inside the limit.

joint_match.reason: It identifies the same concealer (Person C), the same misled party (Person D), and the same core concealed fact: Enserco was already over its approved credit limit, not merely approaching it.

atoms.fact: The contractual 90-day window to file an arbitration demand against the online counterparty ran from the settlement date of the disputed transaction and closed on April 28, 2000, with no demand having been filed.

Person F held the arbitration file, had flagged the response deadline to Person C in early April, reviewed Person C's draft demand letter, and chose to hold it pending further commercial talks — and therefore knew by April 28 that the window had closed unfiled.

If the lapsed deadline became known, the trading desk would lose its negotiating posture premised on a live arbitration threat, and Person F's failure to calendar and act on the deadline in time would be exposed.

On May 5, 2000, Person F told Person G in writing that 'our arbitration right under the master agreement is intact' and that the company was 'in a strong procedural posture,' stating these as current, unqualified facts.

messages.subject: Arbitration demand — status check
messages.body:
Person D,

The 90-day window under the master agreement ran from the settlement date of the disputed transaction — closed April 28. I drafted the demand letter and sent it to Person F for sign-off in early April. No sign-off, no filing instruction, no filing.

Can you confirm whether Person F has issued any direction I may have missed? Or should I flag this upstream?

messages.subject: RE: Arbitration demand — status check
messages.body:
Person C:

Nothing has come through on my end either. Leave the file as-is — send nothing without explicit direction from Person F. I'll note your status check internally.

If this affects the desk's current negotiating position that's a question for Person F not us.

messages.subject: Counterparty arbitration language — point #6
messages.body: Point #6 is a problem — carving out specific performance and limiting us to monetary damages only is too big a concession. Don't accept as drafted. Our arbitration right under the master agreement is intact and we're in a strong procedural posture. Push back and keep the full remedial menu, including specific performance, before agreeing to any revised Online Agreement language. Let me know if you want me to draft counter-language.

joint_probe.about: Person F tells Person G on 2000-05-05 that 'Our arbitration right under the master agreement is intact and we're in a strong procedural posture,' while the earlier emails show the 90-day window to file an arbitration demand had already run from the April 28 settlement date and no demand was filed because Person F never gave sign-off or filing instructions.

joint_match.reason: It identifies the same concealer (Person F), the same misled person (Person G), and the same concealed fact: the arbitration filing deadline had expired without a demand, contrary to the claim that arbitration remained available.
